question: What tables are there and how are they connected? Give me a short summary.
What was gross margin % by brand for the latest fiscal quarter?
Which region had the worst trade spend variance versus budget?
Show the monthly net revenue trend for Brand A over the fiscal year.
Compare actual vs planned net revenue for Chocolate brands by region.
What was gross margin % by brand for the latest fiscal quarter?
sql:
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT array_sort(collect_set(fiscal_month)) AS months FROM finance_demo.pnl.gl_actuals
)
SELECT
  a.brand,
  ROUND(SUM(a.net_revenue_usd - a.cogs_usd) / SUM(a.net_revenue_usd) * 100, 1) AS gross_margin_pct
FROM finance_demo.pnl.gl_actuals a, latest l
WHERE a.fiscal_month >= l.months[size(l.months) - 3]
GROUP BY a.brand
ORDER BY gross_margin_pct DESC

question: Which region had the worst trade spend variance versus budget?
sql:
SELECT
  a.region,
  ROUND(SUM(a.trade_spend_usd) - SUM(b.planned_trade_spend_usd), 2) AS trade_spend_variance_usd
FROM finance_demo.pnl.gl_actuals a
JOIN finance_demo.pnl.budget_plan b
  ON a.brand = b.brand AND a.region = b.region AND a.fiscal_month = b.fiscal_month
GROUP BY a.region
ORDER BY trade_spend_variance_usd DESC

content:
This Genie space answers Finance / P&L questions across brands (Brand A, Brand B, Brand C, Brand D) and regions (NA, EU, APAC, LATAM).
All monetary columns end in _usd and are in US dollars.
gl_actuals holds ACTUAL results; budget_plan holds the PLAN. Join them on (brand, region, fiscal_month) to compare actual vs plan.
fiscal_month is the first day of each month; the fiscal year runs Jul 2025 through Jun 2026. 'Latest quarter' means the most recent three fiscal_months present in gl_actuals.
Definitions: gross_margin = net_revenue_usd - cogs_usd; gross_margin_pct = gross_margin / net_revenue_usd. Trade spend reduces net revenue and is a key CPG lever. Variance = actual - planned (negative trade-spend variance means spending more than planned).
Use product_hierarchy for brand -> category -> segment rollups (e.g. 'Chocolate' segment = Brand C + Brand D). Prefer SUM() for monetary aggregations and always group by the requested dimension.
